thread:
Maya: Heads up — hit a weird edge with the Node sample-runner. When a tool/fncall returns JSON wrapped in triple backticks the SDK's JSON-mode helper doesn't strip the fences before parse. Sample app crashes with SyntaxError. Repro below.

Kevin: Oof. Can you paste the exact response you saw?

Maya: Sure, pasted from logs:```
tool: summarize_article
response: "```json\n{"summary":"short"}\n```"
```

Kevin: Yup, that will blow up if we call JSON.parse on the whole string. Node code path is directly parsing the tool payload.

Ajay: Is this only fenced code blocks? Or also inline code/blockquote quoting?

Maya: Only triple-backtick fences so far. Seen on streaming and non-streaming. Funny thing: Python SDK strips fences before parsing.

CI-bot: Failing CI job: https://ci.internal/runs/7890 — sample-runner/parse-json-mode — stacktrace shows SyntaxError: Unexpected token ` in JSON at position 0.

Lina: Temporary user workaround: set helper.permissiveJson = true (0.13.x) — it tries to peel fences before parse. Not documented though, so onboarding still messy. :face_with_rolling_eyes:

Sam: Proposed fix: add a tiny sanitizer that peels common fences before JSON.parse. Example: ```
function peelFences(s) {
  return s.replace(/^```(?:json)?\n|```$/g, '').trim()
}
```
Also add tests for fenced + indented blocks and CRLF windows line endings.

Ajay: Agreed we need parity across SDKs — if Python strips, Node should too. But be careful: a tool might legitimately start a payload with ``` (rare, but could happen). Add a feature flag and also a strict mode for users who want no-mangling.

Kevin: I'll own the PR. Plan: sanitizer + unit tests + feature flag behind CHG-FN-123. Add an integration test in sample-runner. :shipit:

Maya: Thanks! Assign to Kevin and add a quickstart note so new users don't hit this onboarding friction. @Kevin include a short snippet in the sample app. :bug:

Kevin: Will do. ETA EOD tomorrow.
file_notes: thread about Node SDK JSON parsing when tool responses are fenced code blocks; discusses workaround, CI failure link, proposed sanitizer, parity with Python SDK, and assignment to Kevin
